1. Heard Sri Vijit Saxena, learned counsel for the applicants and Sri Shatrughan Yadav, learned
Aga, for the State.

2. The instant bail application has been filed on behalf of the applicants with the prayer to release
them on bail in S.T.No.679 of 2025 arising out of Case Crime No.20A of 2006, under Sections 409,
420, 467, 468, 471, 477A, 120B and 34 Ipc and Section 13(2) Prevention of Corruption Act, Police
Station Haldi, District Ballia during pendency of the trial.

3.  Learned counsel for the applicants submits that FIR of the present case was lodged in the year 2006 against the applicants and several others and as per allegation applicants and others misappropriated the public fund but entire allegations levelled against the applicants were totally false.

4. He further submits that during investigation applicant along with others approached this Court in Criminal Misc.Writ Petition No. 27939 of 2018 and on 05.10.2018 Division Bench of this Court was pleased to stay their arrest till submission of Police report under Section 173(2) Cr.P.C.
5.

He further submits that pursuant to the order dated 05.10.2018 passed by this Court during investigation applicants were not arrested and they fully cooperated with the investigation but now in the year 2025 charge sheet has been filed and summons were issued to the applicants.
6. He further submits that applicants are having apprehension, if they will appear before the court concerned then then will be sent to jail.

7. He further submits that as during investigation applicants were duly protected and after submission of charge sheet their custodial interrogation is not required, therefore, there is no need to send them in custody.
8.
He further submits that applicants are not having criminal history to their credit.
9. He further submits that therefore, considering the above facts applicants may be enlarged on anticipatory bail till the conclusion of the trial.
10. Per contra, learned AGA although opposed the prayer for bail but could not dispute the argument on facts advanced by the learned counsel for the applicants.
11. I have heard learned counsel for the parties and perused the record of the case.

12. However, as per allegation applicants, who were the public servants, committed offence of misappropriation of public fund along with as many as 80 others but it reflects that during investigation their arrest was stayed by Division Bench of this Court and there is no allegation that Srikant Upadhyay And 2 Others vs State Of U.P. on 6 November, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/90773182/

sentences.text: 2 they did not cooperate with the investigation.
13. Further, now charge sheet has been filed and summons were issued to applicants on 5.8.2025.
Considering this fact, apprehension of arrest raised by the applicants cannot be ruled out.

14. Further, this Court finds merit in the argument advanced by the learned counsel for the applicants that after submission of charge sheet custodial interrogation of the applicants are not required and as applicants were duly protected during investigation, therefore, after submission of charge sheet there is no occasion to send them jail.
15. Further, applicants are not having criminal history to their credit.

16. Therefore, considering the facts and circumstances of the case discussed above, in my view,
applicants are entitled to be released on anticipatory bail till the conclusion of trial.
17. Accordingly, without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case, the instant anticipatory bail application is allowed.

18. In the event of arrest of the applicants-Srikant Upadhyay, Goraksh Nath Singh and Jawahar Prasad Yadav involved in the aforesaid case crime number, shall be released on bail till the conclusion of the trial on furnishing a personal bond with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Presiding Officer/Court concerned with the conditions:-

( i) that the applicants shall not, directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade them from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police officer or tamper with the evidence.
19. In case of breach of any of the above conditions, the court concerned shall have the liberty to cancel the bail granted to the applicants.

20. It is made clear that the observations made in granting anticipatory bail to the applicants shall not in any way affect the learned trial Judge in forming his independent opinion based on the testimony of the witnesses.
